title: Car Rental Rate Classes: What a Renter’s History Across Rentals Decides
content:
The renter's own history across rentals decides two things and nothing else: whether a discretionary waiver is within the desk's authority, and whether the supplier network requires a manual review before the vehicle is released. A renter with more than 2 damage recharges in the last twenty-four months is referred to the rental desk before any discretionary concession is given. Rental days across rentals are counted only to establish a frequent renter's standing; they never change the rate class terms of any single rental. Where two rentals overlap, each is priced, taxed and settled entirely on its own rate class, and a protection product bought on one never extends to the other. Club discounts and corporate rates are likewise applied rental by rental.

**The two matters history decides, and the many it does not.**

*Decided by history.* Whether a discretionary waiver lies within the desk's authority, and whether the supplier network requires a manual review before release.

*Not decided by history.* The terms of any single rental on the Car Rental Rate Classes. Rental days counted across a renter's rentals over the last twelve months establish a frequent renter's standing and nothing further. Pricing, tax and settlement stay with the rate class of the rental they belong to, a protection product bought on one rental stays on that rental, and a club discount or a corporate rate is applied to one rental at a time.

**Boundary on the referral.** The count is of damage recharges in the renter's last twenty-four months. At 2 such recharges the renter is not referred, because the referral turns on a count above the threshold; at 3 the renter is referred to the rental desk before any discretionary concession is given.
